answer.text:
The order type of an opportunity is determined by logic implemented in Salesforce, which classifies every opportunity into one of seven Order Type values. This classification is essential for distinguishing between lands, expansions, contractions, and churn, and it supports accurate commissions, credit & compensation (C&C), and First Order reporting. The "Order Type" field is stamped on the opportunity and is persistent, meaning it remains unchanged even if the opportunity is later lost. There is also an "Order Type Override" field for rare manual corrections, which follows a strict process.

The seven Order Type values are defined in the GTM Technical Documentation, and every opportunity is assigned one of these values based on the implemented logic in Salesforce. This ensures consistency and accuracy across GTM systems and processes for reporting and compensation purposes [sales/field-operations/sales-systems/gtm-technical-documentation/_index#order-type-system] [sales/field-operations/sales-systems/gtm-technical-documentation/_index#order-type-first-orders-gtm-systems-hub] [sales/field-operations/sales-systems/gtm-technical-documentation/_index#dependent-fields-salesforce].

A "first order" is determined by whether the Ultimate Parent Account (UPA) or the UPA plus Domestic Region has had a qualifying first order before, according to the logic for UPA First Order (UPA FO) and Domestic First Order (DFO). Only paid subscriptions (current MRR > 0) count for First Order eligibility; subscriptions with $0 MRR do not make a customer “active” for First Order purposes, do not reset the 180-day timer, and do not block FO/DFO eligibility. The DFO value is also persistent on the opportunity, even if it later moves to Closed Lost [sales/field-operations/sales-systems/gtm-technical-documentation/_index#domestic-first-order-logic-dfo-high-level].

nodes.label: Domestic First Order logic (DFO – high level)
nodes.text:
**Domestic First Order (DFO)** is calculated for **New Business** opportunities:

- Type = New Business.  
- Positive Net ARR.  
- Not storage-only.  
- Not EDU/OSS.  
- Qualifies as a land under the Order Type 2.3 rules (New - First Order / New - Connected / Growth, not Decommission).  
- Is the first such land under the same **UPA and Domestic Region** (Domestic Region account field) within the 180-day policy window.

Key properties:

- Exactly **one UPA FO** at a time per UPA.  
- **Multiple DFOs per UPA are allowed**, but only **one DFO per Domestic Region**.

nodes.label: Order Type System
nodes.text:
**Business process:**  
Classify every opportunity into one of seven Order Type values so we can:

- Distinguish **lands vs expansions vs contractions vs churn**.
- Support accurate **commissions**, **C&C**, and **First Order** reporting.

This section summarizes the implemented logic in Salesforce.

nodes.label: Order Type System
nodes.text:
**Business Process this supports:** [New vs Connected New vs Growth](/handbook/sales/sales-term-glossary/)

**Overview:** The goal of the Order Type system is to determine a given Opportunity's relationship with the business. Did it start a new customer relationship, cross into a related segment of the customer, or grow an existing relationship.
